raw_segments.text: Here, thank you," said the lawyer, and he drew near and leaned on the tall fender.
This hall, in which he was now left alone, was a pet fancy of his friend the doctors,
and Utterson himself was wont to speak of it as the pleasantest room in London.
But tonight there was a shudder in his blood. The face of Hyde sat heavy on his memory.
He felt, what was rare with him, a nausea and distaste of life, and in the gloom of
his spirits, he seemed to read a menace in the flickering of the firelight on the polished
cabinets and the uneasy starting of the shadow on the roof. He was ashamed of his relief,
when Poole presently returned to announce that Dr. Jekyll was gone out.
